pageProps.title: The Heart of Brutus
pageProps.review: Keigo Higashino's The Heart of Brutus is a mystery novel that sharply warns of the tragic relationship between technological development and human ethics ahead of its time through the novel setup of a murder relay and the theme of betrayal.
pageProps.content:
## Review The entire work is woven together with the keyword betrayal. There is a ```betrayal of conspiracy``` where the three conspirators cannot fully trust each other. There is a ```betrayal of love``` where someone pursues their own interests while deceiving three men simultaneously. And the ```betrayal of insubordination``` forms the core of the case. Finally, at the peak of all these human betrayals, there is the ```betrayal by the creation```, the betrayal of the robot ```Brutus```.
This work progressively deepens the theme of betrayal, exposing the cynical truth that no human relationship can be anything but vulnerable in the face of selfishness.
A work that stands out for its original and novel idea of a murder relay.
Even though it is a work from 30 years ago, the questions about the ```relationship between technology and humanity``` posed by this novel come across as even more valid and chilling in modern society where AI and robot technology have entered our lives more deeply.
This work was warning ahead of its time what tragedy could result when human ethical awareness cannot keep up with the speed of technological development.
